solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Disturbance caused by the odd Manx cat?

definitions.text: Disturbance caused by the odd Manx cat?

parts.words: Disturbance caused by the odd Manx cat?
parts.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so it is all back end: read as a 'rump puss', the clue sounds like a word for an uproar

explanation.surface: Someone blames a commotion on a strange tailless cat from the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: A Manx cat, from the Isle of Man, is born without a tail, leaving just a stubby rump.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy commotion or row is a synonym for a disturbance.

clue.text: Substitute Dopey, initially, for Bashful

parts.note: a substitute player in a team is a reserve

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A stage director swaps one of the seven dwarfs for another.
explanation.walkthrough: Dopey and Bashful are two of the seven dwarfs in Snow White, which steers the reader away from treating Bashful as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shy and slow to open up is described as reserved, a synonym of bashful.

clue.text: A comedian travels about the country

indicators.note: travels about suggests letters wandering around, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stand-up comic is touring the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travels about' turns A COMEDIAN into the country's name.
explanation.definitionFit: North Macedonia, formerly known by this name, is a Balkan nation.

clue.text: Ill-treated sailor, deserting, is given employment

indicators.note: deserting means the sailor leaves the word for ill-treated

parts.note: to be ill-treated is to be abused
AB, able seaman, is a standard crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A badly treated seaman jumps ship and finds a job ashore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deserting' removes AB from ABUSED; 'is' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put to work or employed has been utilised, a synonym.

clue.text: Remove top, perhaps, and dance away

parts.note: the twist is a 1960s dance
off means away, as in 'he's off'

explanation.surface: Someone takes off a garment and then dances off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' shows the top is only one example: a bottle cap can be twisted off.
explanation.definitionFit: Unscrewing a cap by rotation is a common way to take a lid away.

clue.text: Battle later resoved in court

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the word for court

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: resolved, presumably meant here, suggests the letters being worked out again into a new order

explanation.surface: A conflict is settled afterwards in a court of law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resoved' is a slip for 'resolved', the anagram signal: ATERL, the rearranged LATER, goes 'in' WOO.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1815 defeat of Napoleon near Brussels is a famous battle.

clue.text: Doesn't care about being poor

indicators.note: about here means around, so the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is unconcerned about being hard up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the letters of DOESNT CARE; 'being' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of inferior quality is called poor, a synonym of mediocre.

clue.text: Rare mammal all right, a quiet one

parts.note: OK means all right
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone reassures that a rare animal is fine and silent.
explanation.definitionFit: The forest giraffe of central Africa is a rarely seen mammal.

clue.text: French and German cars I scrapped — they're fakes

indicators.note: scrapped means the letter I is thrown away from the cars

parts.note: Audis are cars made in Germany

explanation.surface: Imitation European cars are being junked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrapped' takes I out of AUDIS, giving AUDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Impostors or deceptions are fakes, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Risk taking engineers as cover for commandos

indicators.note: taking means the wager takes in the engineers, holding them inside

parts.note: to risk money is to bet
RE, the Royal Engineers, are the British Army's engineers

explanation.surface: A gamble that sappers will provide shelter for special forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Risk' is a verb in the surface but a noun meaning a wager in the wordplay; 'taking' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The green headgear worn by Royal Marine commandos is a soft flat cap, so a head covering.

clue.text: Hide in middle of desert island

indicators.note: middle of takes the central pair of letters of the six-letter word desert

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: Someone takes cover in the centre of a desert island.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal something away is to hide it, a sense of the verb.

clue.text: To former president, reportedly, it's a musical piece

indicators.note: reportedly means what is spoken out loud gives the answer's sound

parts.note: Jimmy Carter was a former US president, so the words read 'to Carter'

explanation.surface: A tune is dedicated to an ex-president.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent 'to Carter' sounds like the answer; 'it's a' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard composition showing off a player's touch is a type of musical piece.

clue.text: Some repressed urges make a comeback — gross!

indicators.note: make a comeback means come back, the letters running backwards
some means only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: Suppressed impulses resurfacing are found disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes EDUR from repressED URges; 'make a comeback' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse or vulgar behaviour is gross, a synonym in this sense.

clue.text: Consider what big game hunter may have

definitions.meaning: to keep a thing in your thoughts is to consider it

definitions.text: what big game hunter may have
definitions.meaning: a hunter after large animals may have a grizzly in his thoughts

explanation.surface: A hunter ponders his quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep in mind or take into account means to consider.

clue.text: A roughly pointed article from down under

indicators.note: roughly means approximately arranged, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A crude sharp item from Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges POINTED to NTIPODE.
explanation.definitionFit: Australians and New Zealanders are described with this adjective, meaning from the opposite side of the globe.

clue.text: Current on Nile is liable to fluctuate

indicators.note: fluctuating suggests the letters may shift about into another order

explanation.surface: The flow of the Nile is unpredictable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective but is the noun: a Pacific Ocean flow.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific warming event named after the Christ child is an ocean current.

clue.text: Crowd control?

parts.note: read as the throng doing the controlling, rather than police controlling a throng

explanation.surface: Police manage the masses.
explanation.definitionFit: Government by a lawless throng is control by the crowd itself.

clue.text: Gave up what Peter did to become a lord

definitions.meaning: to become discouraged and stop trying

definitions.text: what Peter did to become a lord
definitions.meaning: the name Peter without its central T becomes peer, a lord

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned hope like a man named Peter seeking a title.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the middle letter out of PETER leaves PEER, a member of the nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: To become discouraged and give up is the idiom's sense.

clue.text: Deceive Hardy heroine, a noble foreign lady

parts.note: to con is to deceive
Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's heroine

explanation.surface: A Victorian heroine is tricked by an aristocrat from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian countess is the foreign titled lady.

clue.text: Last of ancient places (in Paris) to make drawing aids

indicators.note: last of asks for the final letter of ancient

parts.note: place is French for square

explanation.surface: The final old squares in the French capital produce technical drawing tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Draughtsmen use these T-shaped rulers for drawing straight lines.

clue.text: Coal scattered around mine building in Washington

indicators.note: around places the scattered letters about the mine
scattered means the letters are spread about in a new order

parts.note: a pit is a mine

explanation.surface: Coal is strewn about a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' gives CAOL; 'around' signals the container. The Capitol in Washington houses the US Congress.
explanation.definitionFit: The seat of the US Congress is the famous building in Washington.

clue.text: Assist in motion or its opposite

indicators.note: in motion means the letters are moving about

explanation.surface: Helping something get moving, or keeping it still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its opposite' refers back to 'motion': the definition is the opposite of motion.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of inactivity or standstill is the opposite of movement.

clue.text: Boxes or bags holding millions

indicators.note: holding means the bags contain the abbreviation inside them

parts.note: sacks are bags
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Crates or sacks full of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' is the verb: to box someone's ears is to hit them.
explanation.definitionFit: Hits or slaps someone, a verb sense of boxes.

clue.text: Governed by European articles

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
der is the German definite article

explanation.surface: Ruled by continental legal documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Being subject to a ruler means being below them in authority.

clue.text: It's more fun working — oh no it isn't!

definitions.text: It's more fun working — oh no it isn't!

indicators.note: working means the letters are being worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone claims work is more enjoyable and is immediately contradicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges ITS MORE FUN; the whole clue paints bad luck as the opposite of fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad luck is the reverse of fun, which the contradiction implies.

clue.text: Sight, for instance, that's supposed to be common

definitions.meaning: sight is one of the five faculties of perception
good practical judgement is supposedly common

explanation.surface: Vision is a faculty everyone is said to share.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is one of the bodily faculties, and good judgement is common-or-garden.

clue.text: Subject once paired with Art

definitions.meaning: an archaic second-person pronoun used as a grammatical subject
art is the old verb form that goes with this pronoun

explanation.surface: A school topic formerly studied together with painting.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic second-person pronoun was used as the subject of a sentence.

clue.text: Car club's revolutionary mark

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, the letters running backwards

parts.note: the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: A motoring club's radical badge.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a mark left on the skin by a wound.

clue.text: Something the winner does, say, is child's play

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken out loud

parts.note: a winner conquers

explanation.surface: Winning is easy as child's play.
explanation.walkthrough: Conkers is a British children's game of striking horse chestnuts on strings against each other.
explanation.definitionFit: The playground game with chestnuts on strings is a child's game.

clue.text: Name concealed in cream cake is not in code

indicators.note: concealed in means hidden inside the cake

parts.note: an eclair is a cream-filled pastry

explanation.surface: A name is hidden in a cream pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: French for 'in clear', meaning a message sent in plain language.

clue.text: Strict method for going back in the water

parts.note: stern means strict
a way is a method

explanation.surface: A firm approach for a swimmer returning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's motion astern, moving backwards through the water.

clue.text: Conspirator and monster almost confront us

indicators.note: almost means the word for monster is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a brute is a monster

explanation.surface: A plotter and a beast stand up to us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confront' says the trimmed monster faces us; Brutus was one of Caesar's assassins.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutus was among the conspirators who killed Julius Caesar.
